pr.title: Add field sc voice and field sc notes, and move the voice host to src/sc/voice (sequencer.md chunks 3 and 6)
pr.head: c9ac89015cab3c2c7005749503d593644e65077c

summary: Field plays instruments live through a voice host: a sclang process that boots its own scsynth, loads each instrument's voice, and starts a synth for each MIDI note it receives. Until now only field keys used it, its code lived under src/keys/, and every voice heard every MIDI source on the machine.

The sequencer plan needs other commands to drive voices, and field seq needs a voice that hears only its own track's notes. So this pull request moves the host's TypeScript to src/sc/voice/, gives each voice its own list of MIDI sources, and adds two commands:

• field sc voice plays a track's voice, or an instrument by name or path, from MIDI sources with no keyboard. Each track's voice reaches the song through a daemon input named voice:<song>/<track>.
  • field sc notes runs a SuperCollider program under FIELD_MODE=notes, plays the pattern it answers under a seed, and prints a part to stdout.

It also adds the seq: claim that field seq will use. A session compiled with an input named seq:<song>/<track> leaves out that track's rendered notes, so a part plays once, live. No command opens a seq: input yet.
The living documentation describes both commands, and the plan's §11 records what was settled here. Nobody has run field sc voice by hand with a hardware controller, which the plan still owes.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Voice: one instrument's SynthDef, played live, one synth per sounding note.
  • MIDI source: a named sender of MIDI on the machine, such as a USB controller or the virtual Field Keys.
  • Live input: a named source outside the session that field-audiod, the audio engine, reads every block and carries through a track's effects.
  • FieldOut: the scsynth plugin that writes a voice into a live input's shared-memory ring.
  • Part: a notes file under songs/<song>/notes/, in ticks or bars and beats.
  • Pattern: SuperCollider's description of a sequence of events, such as a Pbind.

cards.title: Where review stands
cards.html:
The gpt-6.1-sol review of this head requests one change: a seq: input removes the claimed notes from the song's natural length, so the transport can stop early. The ten earlier findings are fixed.

The package build, typecheck, focused tests, project checks, and real voice-routing tests passed. The outstanding hardware-controller hand test remains separate from the reproduced length defect.

cards.title: What this leaves for later
cards.html:
• field seq, which publishes the Field Seq sources and opens seq: inputs, is chunk 5 of the plan.
  • Moving this layer lower in the stack is open. The plan says chunks 3 and 4 do not depend on each other, and the pull request body offers the move.
  • Two chunks stay in one pull request, though the plan's §6 asks for one each. The plan's §11 and the pull request body record this.

groups.title: Input names, and the seq: claim
groups.kicker: Two new kinds of live input, and what a seq: input does to a session
intro: A live input is how a voice reaches a song: the voice host writes into a ring that field-audiod reads and carries through the track's effects. Each input's name says which command opened it and which track it belongs to. Any command that reloads a song lists the open inputs by that name, so a reload from field play keeps a voice heard.

The list of names now admits seq: and voice: beside keys: and capture:. Only seq: changes the session. When field seq plays a track's notes live, the track's rendered copy of those notes would play too, so the compile leaves the renders out. The input's name carries this claim, so it needs no new daemon state and it ends when the connection closes.

files.note: Holds the four input kinds. liveInputName replaces captureInputName so every command spells a name the same way.
leaveOutNotes drops each entry that renders notes from a loaded copy of the song, as solo does. The files on disk never change.

checks.text: The session-compile tests passed: a seq: input suppresses the claimed track's part and MIDI take, keeps its audio, and leaves other tracks' notes intact. The test checks the input list but does not check the song's playback length.

files.note: Reads the claim from the input's name and applies it before the graph is built.

checks.text: Solo filters entries by index, so it runs before leaveOutNotes changes that list.

With no declared song length, filtering notes here also removes their contribution to the session's natural extent. An eight-quarter-note part and a 0.1-second audio clip at 120 bpm and 48 kHz compile to 384,000 samples normally but 4,800 with seq:creek/keys. The real daemon stopped the claimed session within 300 ms. Preserve the placements' duration when suppressing their rendered audio.
Both tests passed on macOS. The Windows guard excludes the extensionless test program that sclangCommand refuses on Windows; I checked that guard and the executable lookup code.

files.note: Uses liveInputName. Behavior does not change.
Only an import path changes.

groups.title: Each voice plays from its own MIDI sources
groups.kicker: The voice host stops playing every note on every voice
intro: Before this change, one voicer played every voice from every MIDI source on the machine. A voicer is the object in sc/voicer.scd that turns MIDI into synths and tracks held notes, the pedal, and controllers. Now each voice gets its own voicer and its own list of sources. That list is what lets a field seq voice hear only its track's Field Seq source, and a field keys voice ignore those sources.

The host decides who hears what once, when it starts, from the sources that exist then. A command that publishes a source has to do so before it starts the host, as field keys already does with Field Keys.

files.note: A function from the voices and the machine's sources to two answers: which voices hear each source, and which named source is missing. A name matches a source's name or its device.
Makes one voicer per voice, and sends each MIDI message only to the voicers that hear its source. MIDIClient.init moves up so a missing source fails before scsynth boots.

checks.text: The real-host tests passed for program errors containing a tab, newline, carriage return, quote, and backslash. Each reason reaches the caller without raw @field protocol.
Each source connects inside its own try, so an endpoint that disappears during program loading does not abort host startup. Sources are listed once when the host starts.

Both end-to-end tests passed with real sclang, scsynth, the daemon, and FieldOut. A note reached the track's live input, and two named MIDI sources each drove their own voice without sounding the other input.

files.note: Moved from src/keys/voice-host.ts. It passes each voice's sources in FIELD_INSTRUMENTS, says which voice each trace line is about, and gains reloadOnSave, which both commands use.

checks.text: I traced the extra ..: from src/sc/voice/, or dist/sc/voice/ after a build, three levels up is the package root, so the path still reaches the built plugin under native/.

files.note: Runs sc/voice-sources.scd through real sclang with made-up endpoints, so it publishes no MIDI.

groups.title: The voice library moves to src/sc/voice
groups.kicker: Code that field keys owned becomes code several commands share
intro: This group is mostly a move. Routing, which opens a track's input in field-audiod and reloads the song with it, leaves src/keys/. So do the knob files a voice reads and the SynthDef Field writes for FieldOut.

The real change is in routing: routeVoices takes a required kind, which names the input and the command in its messages. It also asks only for a program and a track, through a small Voice type, so it no longer depends on what field keys resolves.

groups.title: The commands
groups.kicker: field sc voice and field sc notes, and field keys on the shared library
intro: src/commands/sc.ts holds all of field sc: render, moved from src/cli.ts with no change in behavior, and the two new commands. scVoice follows the same steps as field keys without a keyboard or a terminal in raw mode. It resolves the targets, checks the knob files, routes the tracks, starts the host, and watches the files until a signal stops it. Then it closes the host and the inputs.

scNotes runs the pattern harness, described in the next group, and turns what it writes into a part: quarter notes become ticks, a 0-based chan becomes a 1-based channel, and amp times 127 becomes velocity.

files.note: The three field sc commands.

checks.text: The SC-command suite passed all 20 tests, including helper refusal, one host retry on macOS, a second refusal stopping the command, no retry on Linux, and helper closure before host startup. These failure paths use stand-ins rather than a forced real CoreMIDI refusal.
An existing but non-executable FIELD_SCLANG was also checked through the real CLI: it exited 1 and reported EACCES promptly.
All 20 tests passed with a real daemon available and real sclang for notes mode. The voice-command startup and retry cases use the suite's stand-ins.

parseBeats takes any positive number of quarter notes.

groups.title: The pattern harness behind field sc notes
groups.kicker: Plays a program's pattern with no server and writes each note it would sound
intro: A SuperCollider pattern yields a stream of events, each with a pitch, a length, a level, and a time until the next event. sc/notes-render.scd runs the program, seeds the pattern, and pulls events until it reaches the beat --beats gives. It never boots a server, so nothing sounds. It writes each note as JSON, and scNotes in src/commands/sc.ts turns that JSON into a part.
The same seed gives the same bytes, and a part's first line is a comment naming the command that wrote it. So you can edit the part as ordinary text, and the build renders it like any other.

files.note: The harness itself. It runs under FIELD_MODE=notes, and the program's value must be a Pattern.

checks.text: The real sclang tests passed for a pattern that fails during playback and for negative duration. Both stop with the concrete reason rather than waiting for the timeout.
The real pattern tests passed for freq, ctranspose, harmonic, and chords, plus seeded byte reproducibility, channel conversion, sustain, and amplitude.
A separate CLI run of Pbind(\midinote, 60, \dur, Pseq([0.5, Rest(0.5), 0.5], 1)) wrote notes at ticks 0 and 960, preserving the rest.

files.note: runSclang splits out of runScProgram so field sc notes can run the harness and name the user's program in its errors.

checks.text: sclangCommand() now runs inside the try. So a missing sclang reads sclang failed for <program>: sclang not found on PATH …, where it read only the second half before. The advice survives.

groups.kicker: What the living docs now say, and what building this settled
intro: Field keeps docs/ describing how the system works today, so a change that moves behavior updates it in the same pull request. These files add the two commands, the rule for which sources a voice hears, and what a program answers in notes mode.
Plans under docs/projects/ record decisions rather than current behavior. So the sequencer plan gains a section on what chunks 3 and 6 settled, beside the sections on earlier chunks.
